references.text: Isaiah encourages the disheartened to be strong and not fear, for God comes with vengeance and salvation. This encouragement to lift one's eyes in hope of God's saving intervention is reflected in Jesus' words to stand up straight and raise your heads because redemption is near. [ref: Isa 35:3-4|Isaiah 35:3-4]

"Arise, shine! For your light has come" – Isaiah's call to rise in expectation of the Lord's glory corresponds with Jesus' words to stand up straight and raise your heads when redemption is near. [ref: Isa 60:1-2|Isaiah 60:1-2]

Paul writes that we who have the firstfruits of the Spirit eagerly await the redemption of our bodies (apolytrōsis). This final redemption is the same one Jesus points to in Luke 21:28. [ref: Rom 8:23|Romans 8:23]

Paul urges believers not to grieve the Holy Spirit, for they are sealed for the day of redemption (hēmeran apolytrōseōs). This points to the same final redemption that Jesus speaks of. [ref: Eph 4:30|Ephesians 4:30]

The Holy Spirit is the guarantee of our inheritance until the redemption (apolytrōsin) of God's own possession. This future redemption corresponds to what Jesus promises his disciples in Luke 21:28. [ref: Eph 1:14|Ephesians 1:14]
Jesus explains further: When you see these things happening, know that the kingdom of God is near. This clarifies what "redemption" entails – the coming of God's kingdom. [ref: Luke 21:31|Luke 21:31]

Paul writes that we await our Lord Jesus Christ from heaven as Savior, who will transform our lowly body. This expectation of Christ's return and bodily redemption corresponds to the promise in Luke 21:28. [ref: Phil 3:20-21|Philippians 3:20-21]
Christ will appear a second time, not to deal with sin, but to save those who are eagerly waiting for him. This second coming is the redemptive event Jesus speaks of. [ref: Heb 9:28|Hebrews 9:28]

"The ransomed of the Lord shall return and come to Zion with singing." The idea of the Lord's final redemption (ransoming) of his people, with joy and gladness, is the background for Jesus' promise that redemption is near. [ref: Isa 51:11|Isaiah 51:11]

Daniel's vision of the Son of Man coming with the clouds of heaven and receiving dominion, glory, and a kingdom is the immediate context for the signs Jesus describes, and the redemption in verse 28 is linked to the coming of the Son of Man (Luke 21:27). [ref: Dan 7:13-14|Daniel 7:13-14]
